solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Happy to gather copper, type of metal

indicators.note: to gather is to hold something within, so the happy word closes round the copper symbol

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A cheerful metalworker collects copper and talks about kinds of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to gather' puts CU inside MERRY, splitting it MER-CU-RY. 'Copper' and 'metal' both look like the definition; copper only gives its symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is a chemical element, the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.

clue.text: Rate adjusted to accommodate ten more

indicators.note: to accommodate is to make room for, so the reworked letters take the ten symbol inside them
something adjusted has been altered, so the letters of rate are rearranged

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A tariff is changed so that ten more people can be fitted in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' turns RATE into ETRA, and 'to accommodate' puts X inside it: E-X-TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra used as an adjective means additional, beyond the usual amount, which is what more means here.

definitions.meaning: slang for a coward, someone easily frightened
a farmyard bird, so an animal

explanation.surface: A timid creature is described as a scaredy-cat animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is both the domestic fowl and everyday slang for a cowardly person.

clue.text: Cereal in barley recently sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the letters are read from bottom to top, so backwards
in signals that the letters lie inside the words barley recently, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A cereal crop of barley has just been shipped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds EYR across barlEY Recently, and 'sent up' turns it round in this down clue. Barley looks like the cereal, but it is only the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a grain grown for flour and whisky, a cereal like wheat or barley.

parts.note: a can is a tin container

indicators.note: emptied means the inside letters are removed, leaving only the first and last of daddy

explanation.surface: Father's tin of sweets has been emptied out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' strips DADDY down to D and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Candy is the American word for sweets or confectionery.

clue.text: Seed in banana republic to enter Wimbledon, finally

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of each of the five words that come before it

explanation.surface: A seeded player from a banana republic is set to enter Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' applies to every word from banana to Wimbledon: bananA, republiC, tO, enteR, WimbledoN. 'Seed' suggests a tennis seeding but is the botanical seed.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the nut of the oak, containing the seed from which a new tree grows.

indicators.note: something unfortunate has gone wrong, so the letters of act ends are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A poor performance comes to an end with a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A descant is a melody sung or played above the main tune, as in a hymn.

clue.text: Instant trap so designed for dinosaur

parts.note: a trice is an instant, as in 'in a trice'

indicators.note: designed means arranged to a new plan, so the letters of trap so are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A trap is designed to catch a dinosaur in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant' reads as an adjective on the trap but is a noun: TRICE, as in 'in a trice'. 'designed' rearranges TRAP SO into RATOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Triceratops was a large three-horned plant-eating dinosaur of the Cretaceous period.

clue.text: Free and threatening, as a whole

definitions.meaning: an escaped criminal ... is a danger to the public
the public ... means people in general, taken as a whole

explanation.surface: Something is free and menacing, judged as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: At large describes an escaped prisoner still on the loose and posing danger, and also means in general or overall.

definitions.meaning: the part of the body containing the spine

explanation.surface: A brace that supports the spine.
explanation.definitionFit: Back as a verb means to support or endorse, and as a noun is the region of the body along the spine.

parts.note: the idiom for someone near their end is read literally: a thing whose days carry numbers

explanation.surface: A grim warning that someone is close to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: On a wall planner or diary chart, each day of the month is printed with its date number.

parts.note: a crew is a team of staff, as on a ship
cut means trimmed, as hair is

explanation.surface: The workers have had their hair trimmed fashionably.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a very short hairstyle, cropped close on the back and sides.

definitions.meaning: a scrounger who lives off others, as a leech does

explanation.surface: A bloodsucking worm used for cleaning wounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge cleans surfaces, and figuratively a sponger takes from others without giving back, like a parasite.

definitions.meaning: a floating bridge resting on boats or drums
a card game, the British name for twenty-one or blackjack

explanation.surface: Bridge is a game played with cards.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes bridge the card game; here it is a crossing over water, and the card game is the second definition. Pontoon is the British name for blackjack.
explanation.definitionFit: A pontoon is a floating structure supporting a temporary bridge, and also the card game of twenty-one.

clue.text: Fine South coast resort neither opens nor closes

indicators.note: with no opening and no closing, the resort's name loses its first and its final letter

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on the south coast of England

explanation.surface: A fine seaside town on the south coast that never opens or shuts.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON, a seaside town on England's south coast, drops B and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Righto is a casual British exclamation of agreement, meaning okay or all right, just as 'fine' can.

clue.text: Start with support for member, developing flier

parts.note: to go is to start, as in 'ready, steady, go'
a sling supports an injured arm, and an arm is a member, or limb

explanation.surface: A new member of the flying club begins with some backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a club, but it means a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A gosling is a young goose, a bird that will grow into a flier.

clue.text: Icy: uncle slipping about — hard to keep one's balance on this

definitions.text: hard to keep one's balance on this

indicators.note: slipping about suggests things sliding out of place, so the letters of icy and uncle are mixed up

explanation.surface: An uncle slides around on ice, finding it hard to stay upright.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the uncle wobbling about is what riding one is like.
explanation.definitionFit: A unicycle has only one wheel, so the rider must constantly balance to stay upright.

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred
left means remaining, as in 'what is left'

explanation.surface: After a division, one hundred are still there.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleft as an adjective means divided or split, as in a cleft chin.

parts.note: so can mean very, as in 'so tired'

explanation.surface: Something very, very dull.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so describes something mediocre, neither good nor bad.

indicators.note: eaten by means swallowed inside, so the letters sit within the words colossal savage

explanation.surface: A huge brute devours the sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eaten by' finds the letters across colosSAL SAvage.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a spicy Mexican sauce of tomatoes, chilli and onion.

parts.note: the phrase read literally is a climber who has gone beyond the summit, and figuratively someone ageing

explanation.surface: Someone is no longer at their best.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a person too old to perform well, as though they have crossed the top of a hill.

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver to go by how the tree's name is spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: a yew is an evergreen tree; the answer's letters also run across tree we, whether by coincidence or as the setter's bonus, but the parse rests on the sound

explanation.surface: A sheep has got stuck up a tree, so people report.
explanation.walkthrough: YEW and EWE are pronounced the same. As a bonus the answer also sits inside 'tree, we', so the clue works two ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe is the female of the sheep, the term farmers use for breeding stock as opposed to rams.

parts.note: a unit is one, a single thing

indicators.note: firstly asks for just the opening letter of the word end

explanation.surface: Attach one end first.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join together into one.

clue.text: Latvian originally admitted to being a different European

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside, so the Latvian's letter goes into the reworked letters
different means changed, so the letters of being a are rearranged
originally points to the opening letter of Latvian

explanation.surface: A Latvian confesses to actually being from another European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges BEING A (into BEGIAN), and 'admitted to' takes in L from 'Latvian originally'. Latvian looks like the European meant, but it only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Belgian is a person from Belgium, a country in western Europe.
